text.p: Seven analysts polled by Reuters on Monday forecast that Danish biotechnology group Novo Nordisk A/S would post first nine-month 1996 average operational and pre-tax profits around 12 percent higher than in 1995.

The panel forecast operational profits of an average 1.748 billion crowns for the year's first three quarters, 11 percent up on 1995's 1.576 billion, with estimates spanning from 1.726 to 1.785 billion crowns.
It saw the period's pre-tax profit 12 percent up at 1.852 billion crowns on average, with the most positive estimate at 1.890 billion crowns, the least optimistic at 1.817 billion.
The pre-tax profit figure compared with end-September 1995's 1.656 billion crowns.
Turnover was seen rising by a modest four percent to 10.670 billion crowns for the nine-month period.
Novo unveils its 1996 first nine-month result on Wednesday November 13. The panel's forecasts fit with Novo's own earlier expectations of 10-15 percent higher 1996 full year operational profits.
